examples.ko: 올해는 비가 안 와서 쭉정이만 가득해요.
examples.en: It didn't rain this year, so there is nothing but empty husks.
Please pick out the empty husks and collect only the good grain.
I threshed the rice and there are too many empty husks.

examples.ko: 겉만 번지르르하고 속은 쭉정이 같은 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people look shiny outside but are hollow inside.

examples.ko: 이 콩은 다 쭉정이라서 먹을 게 없어요.
examples.en: These beans are all empty husks, so there is nothing to eat.

examples.ko: 바람에 쭉정이를 날려 보내고 쌀만 남겼어요.
examples.en: I blew the husks away in the wind and kept only the rice.

explain: 속에 알맹이가 없는 곡식을 말하고, 반대말은 '알곡'이나 '알맹이'예요. 사람이나 물건이 겉만 그럴듯하고 속이 비었다고 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to grain with no kernel inside, and its opposites are '알곡' and '알맹이'. It is also used figuratively for people or things that look fine outside but are hollow inside.

examples.en: Grandma tuts when she sees how I look.
The man next to me walked past, clicking his tongue in disapproval.

examples.ko: 왜 자꾸 쯧쯧거리세요? 제가 뭘 잘못했어요?
examples.en: Why do you keep tutting? Did I do something wrong?
My father tutted while watching the news.

examples.ko: 친구가 쯧쯧거리는 소리가 들려서 기분이 안 좋았어요.
examples.en: I heard my friend tutting and it made me feel bad.

examples.ko: 사람들이 쯧쯧거려도 저는 신경 안 써요.
examples.en: Even if people tut at me, I don't care.

explain: 안타깝거나 못마땅할 때 혀를 차며 내는 소리를 반복한다는 말이에요. 보통 '혀를 차다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 상대 앞에서 쯧쯧거리면 무시하는 느낌을 줄 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes repeatedly clicking your tongue out of pity or disapproval. People more often say '혀를 차다'. Tutting in front of someone can come across as dismissive.

examples.en: I accidentally stepped on the can and crushed it.
Be careful not to squash the box.
The child squashes the paper cup with his hand.
I almost dented the car next to me while parking.

examples.ko: 화가 난 그는 종이를 찌그러뜨려 던졌어요.
examples.en: Angry, he crumpled the paper and threw it.
If you squash the hat, it won't go back into shape.

explain: '찌그러지다'는 저절로 모양이 망가지는 것이고, '찌그러뜨리다'는 누군가 힘을 가해 그렇게 만드는 거예요. '찌그러트리다'로도 쓸 수 있어요. 캔이나 상자처럼 단단한 물건에 자주 써요.
explain_en: '찌그러지다' means something loses its shape by itself, while '찌그러뜨리다' means someone applies force to make that happen. '찌그러트리다' is also an accepted form. It is often used for fairly hard objects such as cans and boxes.

examples.en: My foot has gone numb, so my leg is tingling.
My heart tingled at the moving scene.
My teeth tingle after drinking cold water.
I keep having a tingling feeling in my hand.
The tip of my nose tingled and then tears came.
Maybe I touched something electric, because my arm is tingling and hurts.

explain: 몸이 저릴 때뿐 아니라 감동으로 가슴이나 코끝이 울릴 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 몸이 저리면 '저리다', 마음이 움직이면 '뭉클하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used both for a numb, tingling body and for the stir of emotion in your chest or nose. In everyday talk people more often say '저리다' for numbness and '뭉클하다' for being moved.

examples.en: My leg tingles when I stand up after sitting for a while.
My fingertips tingled because of static electricity.

examples.ko: 허리를 숙이면 어깨가 찌릿한 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: When I bend over, I get a tingling feeling in my shoulder.
My arm tingles and I can't put any strength into it.
I knelt for a long time and now my toes are tingling.

examples.ko: 문 손잡이를 잡자 찌릿한 전기가 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I grabbed the door handle, I felt a tingling shock.

explain: 저리거나 전기가 오는 것처럼 몸이 울리는 느낌에 주로 써요. '짜릿하다'는 스릴이나 쾌감처럼 기분 좋은 자극에도 쓰지만, '찌릿하다'는 몸의 느낌에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for a numb or electric-like sensation in the body. '짜릿하다' can also describe a pleasant thrill, but '찌릿하다' is closer to a physical feeling.

examples.en: I couldn't say a word in front of my senior.
The children are sitting without making a sound.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 부장님 앞에서는 찍소리 못 해요.
examples.en: That person can't say a peep in front of the department head.

examples.ko: 억울해도 찍소리 한 번 안 하고 참았어요.
examples.en: Even though it was unfair, I endured it without a single complaint.
Why didn't you at least say something?

examples.ko: 혼날까 봐 찍소리 안 하고 방에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Afraid of being scolded, I went into my room without a peep.

explain: 거의 항상 '찍소리 못 하다', '찍소리 없이'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써요. 눌려서 불평이나 말 한마디 못 하는 상황이 떠오르는 말이에요. 약간 속된 느낌이라 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: I couldn't say a word in front of my boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 눌려서 아무 말도 못 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is so intimidated they cannot say anything.
phrases.en_equiv: not dare to say a peep

explain_en: It is almost always used with negatives, as in '찍소리 못 하다' or '찍소리 없이'. It paints a picture of someone too intimidated to say a single word. It sounds a bit colloquial, so it is rarely used in formal settings.

examples.en: It rained just a little and then stopped.
Water only dribbles out of the faucet.
I shed a few tears while watching the movie.

examples.ko: 월급을 찔끔 올려 줘서 별로 기쁘지 않아요.
examples.en: They raised my pay only a tiny bit, so I'm not very happy.
Add just a little dash of soy sauce.

examples.ko: 용돈을 찔끔씩 주지 말고 한 번에 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't give me allowance in tiny bits; give it all at once.

explain: 액체가 조금 새어 나오거나 돈, 일을 조금씩 할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 돈이나 일에 쓰면 너무 적다는 못마땅한 느낌이 들어요. 반복해서 '찔끔찔끔'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a liquid leaking out in small amounts, or money or work being given in tiny portions. Used for money or work, it carries a feeling of dissatisfaction that it is too little. It can also be repeated as '찔끔찔끔'.

examples.ko: 오월이 되면 산길에 찔레꽃이 하얗게 피어요.
examples.en: When May comes, wild roses bloom white along the mountain path.
The scent of wild roses was carried in on the wind.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 찔레꽃 핀 길로 학교에 다녔어요.
examples.en: As a child I went to school along a path where wild roses bloomed.

examples.ko: 할머니는 찔레꽃을 보면 고향이 생각난다고 하세요.
examples.en: Grandma says wild roses remind her of her hometown.

examples.ko: 담장 옆에 찔레꽃 한 그루가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A wild rose bush stands beside the fence.
I like people who are simple like wild roses.

explain: 찔레나무에 피는 작은 꽃으로, 흰색이 많고 늦봄에 피어요. 정원의 장미와 달리 산과 들에서 저절로 자란다는 느낌이 있어요. 시나 노랫말에서 소박함이나 그리움을 나타낼 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the small flower of the wild rose bush, often white and blooming in late spring. Unlike garden roses, it gives the feeling of growing naturally in hills and fields. It often appears in poems and song lyrics to evoke simplicity or longing.

examples.en: Seawater tastes salty.
Tears got into my mouth, so it tasted salty.
Sweat ran down and the corner of my mouth tastes salty.
The broth was salty, so I drank a lot of water.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 단맛 뒤에 찝찔한 맛이 나요.
examples.en: This snack has a salty taste after the sweetness.
I went to the beach and now my hair feels salty.

explain: 바닷물, 눈물, 땀처럼 약간 짭짤하면서 개운하지 않은 맛이나 느낌을 말해요. 음식 간이 센 것을 말할 때는 보통 '짜다'를 써요. 맛있는 짠맛보다는 별로 반갑지 않은 짠맛에 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes a faintly salty and slightly unpleasant taste or feel, like seawater, tears or sweat. For food that is too heavily seasoned, people usually say '짜다'. It suits an unwelcome saltiness rather than a tasty one.

examples.en: My friend looked at me and winked.
The child laughs, scrunching up his nose.
The teacher gave a wink as if to say it was okay.
Try scrunching just one eye, like a wink.
My younger sibling twitched their mouth and then laughed secretly.
I have a habit of scrunching up my nose.

explain: 눈, 코, 입을 살짝 움직이는 동작인데 장난스럽거나 귀여운 느낌이 있어요. '눈을 찡긋하다'는 윙크나 눈짓으로 신호를 보낼 때 많이 써요. '찡그리다'는 불편해서 얼굴을 구기는 것이라 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes a slight movement of the eyes, nose or mouth, usually with a playful or cute feel. '눈을 찡긋하다' is commonly used for a wink or a signal with the eyes. '찡그리다' means frowning in discomfort, so the feeling is different.

examples.en: Tax is deducted from the salary.
I got my deposit back after the repair cost was deducted.

examples.ko: 이번 달 급여에서 식비를 차감하겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said they would deduct the meal cost from this month's pay.

examples.ko: 쿠폰 금액을 차감한 가격이 최종 금액이에요.
examples.en: The price after deducting the coupon amount is the final amount.

examples.ko: 지각할 때마다 점수를 차감하면 학생들이 불안해해요.
examples.en: If you deduct points every time students are late, they get anxious.
You have to deduct the fee when giving a refund.

explain: '빼다'보다 격식 있는 말로, 돈이나 점수를 계산에서 뺄 때 써요. 반대말은 '가산하다'예요. 명세서나 계약서에서 자주 보이고, '포인트가 차감돼요'처럼 피동 표현도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '빼다', used when subtracting money or points in a calculation. Its opposite is '가산하다'. You often see it on statements and contracts, and the passive form is common, as in '포인트가 차감돼요'.

examples.en: In this lesson, we learn greetings.
The thing to bring for the next lesson is colored pencils.

examples.ko: 한 차시는 보통 사십 분에서 오십 분이에요.
examples.en: One lesson period is usually forty to fifty minutes.

examples.ko: 이 단원은 모두 다섯 차시로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This unit is made up of five lessons in total.

examples.ko: 지난 차시에 배운 내용을 복습해 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we review what we learned in the last lesson?

examples.ko: 두 차시 연속으로 수업이 있어서 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have two lessons in a row, so it's tiring.

explain: 수업 한 번 한 번을 순서대로 세는 단위로, 보통 '1차시', '2차시'처럼 숫자와 함께 써요. '교시'는 하루 시간표에서 몇 번째 시간인지를 말하고, '차시'는 한 단원 안의 수업 순서를 말할 때 써요. 학교나 교육 자료에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It counts each class in order and is usually used with numbers, like '1차시' or '2차시'. '교시' tells which period it is in the daily timetable, while '차시' gives the order of lessons within a unit. You see it a lot in schools and teaching materials.

examples.en: The bank seized my salary account.
A seizure notice was stuck on the house.

examples.ko: 차압이 들어오기 전에 빚을 갚아야 해요.
examples.en: I have to pay off the debt before the seizure comes.
He hid his assets to avoid seizure.
I consulted a lawyer about the seizure.
I was shocked to receive a seizure notice.

explain: 빚을 못 갚을 때 재산을 마음대로 팔지 못하게 묶어 두는 것을 말해요. 법률에서는 보통 '압류'라고 하지만, '차압 딱지'처럼 일상에서 아직 쓰는 표현도 있어요. 뉴스나 드라마에서 빚 이야기가 나올 때 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means freezing someone's property so they cannot sell it freely when they cannot repay a debt. In legal terms '압류' is usually used, but '차압' lives on in everyday phrases like '차압 딱지'. You may hear it in news or dramas about debt.

examples.en: I put an awning over the window and now it's cool.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 차양 아래에서 비를 피했어요.
examples.en: I took shelter from the rain under the awning in front of the shop.
The sunlight was strong, so I put up an awning.

examples.ko: 모자 차양이 넓어서 얼굴이 안 타요.
examples.en: The brim of my hat is wide, so my face doesn't tan.

examples.ko: 차양이 접혀 있어서 햇빛이 그대로 들어와요.
examples.en: The awning is folded, so the sunlight comes straight in.
Thanks to the awning, the yard is shaded.

explain: 창문이나 가게 앞에 햇빛과 비를 가리려고 달아 놓은 지붕 같은 것이에요. 모자 앞쪽에 튀어나온 부분을 '차양'이라고 하기도 하지만, 일상에서는 보통 '챙'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a roof-like cover hung over a window or shop front to block sun and rain. The projecting front part of a hat can also be called '차양', but in daily life people usually say '챙'.

examples.ko: 차용증 같은 사문서에도 서명 날짜를 꼭 적어 두세요.
examples.en: Be sure to write the signing date even on private documents like an IOU.

examples.ko: 빌려준 돈을 받을 채권이 있다는 걸 증명하려면 차용증이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need an IOU to prove you have a claim to the money you lent.

examples.ko: 친구 사이여도 큰돈을 빌릴 때는 차용증을 써야 해요.
examples.en: Even between friends, you should write an IOU when borrowing a large sum.
I wrote the repayment date and interest on the IOU.
The person who lent the money keeps the IOU.

examples.ko: 차용증 없이 돈을 빌려줬다가 받기 어려워졌어요.
examples.en: I lent money without an IOU and now it's hard to get it back.

explain: 돈을 빌렸다는 사실과 금액, 갚을 날짜를 적은 문서예요. 쓰는 사람은 돈을 빌린 사람이고, 보관은 빌려준 사람이 해요. '차용증을 쓰다', '차용증을 받다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a document recording that money was borrowed, the amount and the repayment date. The borrower writes it and the lender keeps it. Common phrases are '차용증을 쓰다' and '차용증을 받다'.

examples.en: I sold the stock and made a profit.
House prices rose, so the profit from the sale was large.

examples.ko: 이번 거래로 얻은 차익은 생각보다 작았어요.
examples.en: The profit from this deal was smaller than I expected.
Tax is also charged on the profit.
It's risky to invest only to chase a quick gain.
Most of the profit went to taxes.

explain: 사고판 값의 차이로 생기는 이익이라서 '매매 차익', '시세 차익'처럼 써요. 그냥 '이익'은 어디에나 쓰지만 '차익'은 산 값과 판 값의 차이를 강조해요. 주로 주식, 부동산, 환율 뉴스에서 들어요.
explain_en: It is the gain that comes from the difference between buying and selling prices, as in '매매 차익' and '시세 차익'. While '이익' can be used for any profit, '차익' stresses that difference. You mostly hear it in news about stocks, real estate and exchange rates.

examples.en: The company increased its borrowing from the bank.
There is a lot of borrowing, so the interest burden is heavy.
The amount borrowed is growing every year.

examples.ko: 차입으로 마련한 돈이라 꼭 갚아야 해요.
examples.en: This is borrowed money, so I must pay it back.
I heard the government decided not to rely on borrowing.
Borrowing from a bank was not as easy as I thought.

explain: 회사나 정부가 돈을 빌려 오는 일을 말할 때 많이 써요. 개인이 은행에서 돈을 빌릴 때는 보통 '대출', 가볍게는 '빌리다'라고 해요. 경제 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when a company or government borrows money. For an individual borrowing from a bank, people usually say '대출', or casually '빌리다'. It appears often in economic news and articles.
